wiki_paras: Christa Pike was the most-read article on Wikipedia, with 1,334,670 views. The 2026 Asian Games medal table came second with 363,735. The gap is a factor of 3.7, wide enough that the runner-up would need to nearly quadruple to catch the leader. It did not.

Nothing in the snapshot explains it. No topic formed a cluster across feeds, and none of the Hacker News, Lemmy, Bluesky or Mastodon items mention her. Cornell 7 sits fourth with 261,954 views, also unattached to any news item here. The reason is evidently held by a million readers and shared with none of our feeds.

The rest of the top five is orderly by comparison. The Asian Games occupy three places: the medal table, India's page, and the main event at 254,153 views. Added together, those three pages reach 961,510 views, which is still short of the leader. One name outran an entire sporting event.
letter_paras: The snapshot is scattered, with one loud exception. Wikipedia produced a clear winner, 3.7 times ahead of second place, but no other feed picked it up. Elsewhere the day was ordinary: Hacker News gave Gemini 4 Argon 1,166 points, Counter-Strike 2 held 1,316,372 peak players, and Taylor Swift led YouTube with 5,610,621 views.

In the unglamorous corners, Hugging Face lists a model called laya with 0 downloads, while TeleOCR has 30,383. Mastodon contributed an abandoned New Jersey mall, the Phillipsburg Mall, open from 1989 to 2020. Cloudflare's busiest domains are google.com, googleapis.com, gstatic.com, amazonaws.com and apple.com, which is to say the plumbing.

Taking every feed in the same hour keeps the comparison honest. A topic that appears everywhere is a story; one that appears in a single place is a habit of that place. Today the method returned a clean negative, no shared subject across seventeen feeds, and a negative is worth having on record.
